prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from bifunctional PROTACs to the molecular mechanism of thalidomide-type glue degraders

statement.case_for: After the first round, my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part prize for targeted protein degradation by induced proximity (B057), credited to Crews, Deshaies and Handa. The scientific core is a new chemical mode of action. A small molecule brings a target and an E3 ligase together and the cell's own degradation machinery does the work, catalytically and with event-driven rather than occupancy-driven pharmacology. The mechanism, covering ternary-complex formation, E3 recruitment and cereblon as the thalidomide target, is confirmed in many independent laboratories, and no member who discussed B057 disputed that. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional strategy, and Handa's identification of cereblon explains why thalidomide-type drugs work and links the glue strand to the PROTAC strand through one mechanism. That is the reason I keep Handa as the third name: cereblon is the discovery that makes the field one subject and not two. Five of eight members state this same configuration, and it is the first alternative of the other three, but I treat that as a reason to test the case more carefully, not as a substitute for it. The two timing and attribution objections have been answered sufficiently for me: the committee has not required an approved drug when mechanism and generality are established, and the three-name cap, though costly, produces a citation that is accurate.
statement.case_against: No degrader is approved, so the objection that the field is a few years early remains real, and I do not dismiss it. Credit spreads over at least eight people, and the three-name cap leaves out Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Ito and Kim, each with a genuine claim; Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are real chemistry that this configuration does not credit by name. The citation has to cover both PROTACs and glues without implying that the glue strand was designed, which it was not. If the committee finds this blurring unacceptable, or wants a fully validated result, B054 (Schultz, Chin, Wang) is the cleaner and safer prize, and B068 (Buchwald, Hartwig) is the most mature and the cleanest in attribution but sits closest to an area already honoured in 2010.

responses.point: Brzezinski prefers B054 (Schultz, Chin, Wang) on grounds of maturity, absence of a clinical-validation question and a coherent three-person split, and still treats Handa versus Ciulli as unsettled for B057.
responses.response: I take the maturity argument seriously, and B054 is my first alternative for that reason. Genetic code expansion is stable, reproduced for two decades and cleanly divided between concept (Schultz, Wang) and generalisation (Chin). My difficulty is not quality but novelty of mode of action and fit with the last decade: 2018, 2020 and 2024 all went to biomolecular engineering tools, and you yourself list that as a concern. On Handa versus Ciulli I have decided, and I keep Handa. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made PROTACs drug-like, but that is a refinement inside the PROTAC strand, whereas cereblon explains the thalidomide puzzle and unites both strands. I would not drop Deshaies for Ciulli, because that would turn the citation into a PROTAC-only prize and leave the glue and cereblon strand unattributed, and I do not think we can honour Ciulli without that cost.

responses.point: Somfai and Zou argue that C-N coupling (B068) is a general, mature and cleanly attributed method distinct from the 2010 C-C coupling prize, and Somfai asks for the committee to weigh generality and priority clarity against novelty.
responses.response: The chair's question, and Peter's own answer, is the best statement of the B068 case: C-N coupling is chemically distinct from C-C coupling, because amine binding and C-N reductive elimination are different mechanistic problems, and the ligand design that solved them is real conceptual work. I accept that the attribution to Buchwald and Hartwig is cleaner than anything in B057. Where I remain unpersuaded is the weight. A second cross-coupling prize within sixteen years, with Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work still unresolved in the priority narrative, is a harder position to defend than a new modality. I would not call it a flaw, and I keep B068 as my second alternative. I would change if the committee judged that clean priority and decades of industrial validation should outweigh breadth, but I do not hold that view myself.

responses.point: Zou asks that a B068 citation make explicit that the catalytic, ligand-controlled general method is the basis for crediting Buchwald and Hartwig, and that Kosugi be handled with care.
responses.response: That is a reasonable wording requirement and it shows that B068 can be written precisely: the citation would credit the general catalytic method, not the first stoichiometric amination. It does not remove my reservation about a second cross-coupling prize, and it does not make Kosugi's role simpler. I also note that B057 faces a parallel wording task, where the citation must say what each strand contributed, and I think the current wording does that.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B057 first with the Crews, Deshaies and Handa cut, would accept B054 if B057 is judged premature, and ranks base editing (B016) in his top three with a Liu-centred attribution.
responses.response: I agree on the cut and on the timing worry. Where I changed my mind slightly is on B016: in round 1 I kept it as an alternative; having read the exchange I now rank it below B068 as a fallback, since three members raised that base editing adds less beyond the 2020 genome-editing prize and its off-target and safety data are still maturing. Your suggestion to pair it with prime editing is sensible but would put Liu in a configuration that is not on the shortlist, so it is not available to us. For the committee's fallback question, my order is B054 first, then B068.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will award before any degrader drug is approved
Whether the three-name cap, without Ciulli, can be defended as an accurate representation of the PROTAC lineage
Whether the shared citation for PROTACs and glues is read as one achievement or as a blur of two
Whether the 2018, 2020 and 2024 biomolecular-tool prizes weigh against B054 as the fallback
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. No candidate on the shortlist is a documented collaborator or Lund colleague. As chair I note that fellow Lund academics Somfai and Sparr, and Stockholm University colleagues Brzezinski and Zou, sit on the committee, but none of this bears on a named candidate and I do not request recusal.
